questions.q: What does Field-Level Security (FLS) control that object permissions alone don't?
options: Whether a user can see the object's tab in the navigation bar
Whether a user can see or edit one specific field, independent of their object-level access
Which records a user owns
Which app a user logs into by default
questions.explain: FLS goes one level narrower than object permissions, restricting a single specific field regardless of the user's overall object access.

questions.q: What are the two independent checkboxes FLS sets per field, per profile or permission set?
options: Create Access and Delete Access
View All and Modify All
Read Access and Edit Access
Public Access and Private Access
questions.explain: FLS is set with Read Access and Edit Access as two independent checkboxes per field.

questions.q: Why do fields like Owner, Created By, and Last Modified By show greyed-out, locked checkboxes in the Field Permissions table?
options: They are custom fields that haven't been activated yet
They are system fields FLS structurally can't restrict
They belong to a different object and were included by mistake
They require a premium Salesforce license to unlock
questions.explain: The lesson explains these are system fields Salesforce always needs to report, so FLS can't restrict them.

questions.q: What happens if an admin unchecks Read Access on a field that currently has Edit Access checked?
options: Nothing changes -- Edit Access stays checked independently
Salesforce throws a deployment error and blocks the save
Edit Access is cleared along with Read Access, since you can't edit a field you can't see
Read Access re-enables itself automatically after a few minutes
questions.explain: The FLS UI enforces that Edit Access always implies Read Access, so unchecking Read Access clears Edit Access too.

questions.q: Besides editing FLS from a profile or permission set, where else can an admin set it, per this lesson?
options: Only through the Salesforce CLI, never through the UI
From the field itself in Object Manager, via Set Field-Level Security
From the Role Hierarchy setup page
From the Organization-Wide Defaults sharing settings page
questions.explain: Set Field-Level Security, reachable from the field in Object Manager, shows every permission set/profile touching that object for quick, field-first configuration.
